title: US measles cases hit 2,318 in 2026, surpassing last year's total: CDC
snippet:
The majority of measles cases in 2026 have been confirmed among children and teenagers aged 19 and younger, according to the CDC. About one in 10 children under age 5 have been hospitalized.

About 93% of cases are among people who are unvaccinated or whose vaccination status is unknown, CDC data shows. [...] Previously, last year's total of 2,289 was the highest number of recorded measles cases in more than 30 years, CDC data shows. The new figure marks the highest number of cases recorded since 1991.

Cases have been confirmed in 43 states and the District of Columbia. Sixteen of this year's total have been among international visitors to the U.S., according to the CDC. [...] Meanwhile, 3% of cases are among those who have received just one dose of the measles, mumps, rubella (MMR) vaccine and 4% of cases are among those who received the recommended two doses, according to the CDC.

title: U.S. measles cases hit 35-year record with months left in 2026
snippet:
# U.S. measles cases hit 35-year record with months left in 2026

Data from Johns Hopkins University’s U.S. measles tracker shows the nation reported 2,295 cases as of Tuesday. That count surpasses last year’s total of 2,289.

The United States has now reported the most measles cases in any year since 1991, not only surpassing all of last year’s record total, but also reaching the highest level in 35 years, with more than five months still remaining in 2026.

title: Measles
snippet:
WHO continues to strengthen the Global Measles and Rubella Laboratory Network (GMRLN) to ensure timely diagnosis of measles and track the virus’ spread to assist countries in coordinating targeted vaccination activities and reduce deaths from this vaccine-preventable disease.

### The IA2030 Measles & Rubella Partnership [...] Before the introduction of measles vaccine in 1963 and widespread vaccination, major epidemics occurred approximately every two to three years and caused an estimated 2.6 million deaths each year.

An estimated 95 000 people died from measles in 2024 – mostly children under the age of five years, despite the availability of a safe and cost-effective vaccine. [...] Routine measles vaccination, combined with mass immunization campaigns in countries with high case rates are crucial for reducing global measles deaths. The measles vaccine has been in use for about 60 years and costs less than US$ 1 per child. The measles vaccine is also used in emergencies to stop outbreaks from spreading. The risk of measles outbreaks is particularly high amongst refugees, who should be vaccinated as soon as possible.

title: Immunization coverage
snippet:
Measles is a highly contagious disease caused by a virus, which usually results in a high fever and rash, and can lead to blindness, encephalitis or death. By the end of 2025, 84% of children had received 1 dose of measles-containing vaccine by their second birthday, and 77% of children received 2 doses of measles vaccine. By the end of 2025, 192 Member States had included a second dose of measles vaccine in their national immunization schedules. [...] Measles, because of its high transmissibility, acts as an early warning system, quickly exposing immunity gaps in the population. Still, nearly 21 million children missed their routine first dose of measles, far from the 2019 level of 19 million.

## Global immunization coverage 2025

A summary of global vaccination coverage in 2025 follows. [...] Rubella is a viral disease which is usually mild in children, but infection during early pregnancy may cause fetal death or congenital rubella syndrome, which can lead to defects of the brain, heart, eyes and ears. Rubella vaccine was introduced in 179 Member States by the end of 2025, including one at the subnational level, and global coverage was estimated at 73%.
